title: Install critical PHP safety update or go offline, cyber chiefs tell websites
body:
# Cyber chiefs tell websites to make critical safety update or go offline

Getty Images Hands on a computer keyboard

Organisations which rely on the PHP programming language are being told they should install a significant software update today - or consider taking their websites offline.

Two critical vulnerabilities with PHP, which is widely used across the internet, have been identified.

The PHP Foundation, which supports it, is issuing updates which address them on Wednesday afternoon. [...] The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes as soon as they become available.

The Netherlands' cyber-security agency says it is taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities identified.

The country's National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. [...] "PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cybersecurity company Huntress said.

The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution".

title: PHP2Shell: Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619) Explained
body:
PHP shipped an out-of-cycle security release on October 21, 2026, for two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which its security team rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 (Critical). The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Researchers call the pair php2shell. Both are unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in PHP’s core, and the release was pulled forward a day after details leaked ahead of the embargo. PHP is explicit that there is no complete mitigation: updating is the [...] One rapid-response scan counted roughly 884,000 internet-facing hosts reporting PHP 8.1 or older on October 20, about 59% of the ~1.5 million that reported any version, with a further 740,000 reporting PHP with no version at all. These are banners, not confirmed-vulnerable systems, but they map the scale. [...] CVE-2026-109618 RCE via OOM corruption

In vulnerable PHP versions, an out-of-memory (OOM) error can trigger `longjmp()`, abruptly interrupting request processing while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then act on that invalid data, potentially enabling remote code execution. The confirmed mod\_php attack occurs before application code runs; other server interfaces can have different attack prerequisites.

title: Primus Partners calls for 6 policy interventions to drive AI in Indian agri - BusinessLine
body: # Primus Partners suggests policy interventions for AI adoption in Indian agriculture. ## Policy report proposes six policy interventions aimed at building trust, inclusivity and accountability into India’s agricultural AI ecosystem. Primus Partners has released a policy report — ‘6 Policy interventions needed for the cognitive revolution in agriculture’ — outlining a roadmap to accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) across India’s agricultural ecosystem. While initiatives such as the IndiaAI Mission, Digital Agriculture Mission and AgriStack have laid the foundation for a data-rich agricultural ecosystem, the report identifies an emerging ‘crisis of intelligence’ where vast amounts of agricultural data are yet to be converted into actionable insights at the farm level. The report proposes six policy interventions aimed at building trust, inclusivity and accountability into India’s agricultural AI ecosystem. According to the report, women account for nearly 40-45 per cent of India’s agricultural workforce but continue to face barriers in accessing digital services and AI-enabled platforms.

## AMD vs LRCX: Contrasting Paths in the AI Semiconductor Surge

AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) designs central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), and AI accelerators, while LRCX (Lam Research) supplies the wafer-fabrication equipment used to build advanced chips. AMD has delivered strong double-digit revenue growth on AI data-center demand, but its shares trade with elevated expectations that can trigger sharp reactions around earnings. [...] Advanced Micro Devices and Intel Corporation remain two of the most closely watched semiconductor stocks as artificial intelligence continues to reshape demand for computing chips. Comparing them essentially means weighing two distinct approaches to the same infrastructure expansion. This comparison helps when evaluating relative performance, positioning, and momentum, since both compete in server CPUs yet follow very different strategies, profitability paths, and valuation setups. [...] AMD is a large-cap designer of CPUs (central processing units) and GPUs (graphics processing units) competing directly with Nvidia in the AI accelerator market, while FORM is a small-cap provider of semiconductor test and measurement equipment, primarily probe cards. AMD's narrative has been driven by multi-billion-dollar hyperscaler deals, while FORM's has been powered by record revenue and sharp margin expansion tied to high-bandwidth memory (HBM) demand.

title: The AI factory is becoming the computer and it’s changing the semiconductor race - SiliconANGLE
body:
Papermaster made the case that broad-purpose CPUs and GPUs aren’t going away. Instead, modular architectures and chiplets allow semiconductor suppliers to create workload-specific variations while retaining common foundations. AMD’s multiple Venice designs are an example of that approach, including configurations increasingly tailored toward emerging agentic workloads.

At the other end of the spectrum are custom accelerators. [...] The semiconductor industry is entering a new phase of the artificial intelligence buildout, and I think the market is still underestimating how profound the architectural change will be.

For the first several years of generative AI, the conversation centered on the accelerator. GPUs were the scarce resource, Nvidia Corp. became the defining company of the AI infrastructure cycle, and everyone wanted to know how many GPUs could be obtained and how quickly they could be deployed. [...] GPUs become scarce. Capacity responds. Then HBM becomes scarce. Packaging becomes constrained. Networking gets stressed. Transformer and power capacity become the gating factor. Then cooling, land and permitting enter the equation. As one constraint gets solved, pressure moves somewhere else in the AI factory.
